subject: Geography
description: Iron-steel locations, cotton textile, sugar belt, IT clusters, automotive hubs

questions.stem: India's first iron and steel plant in the modern era — Tata Iron and Steel Co. (TISCO) — was set up in 1907 at:

options.option_text: Burnpur, West Bengal
Sakchi, later renamed Jamshedpur (Jharkhand)
Bhilai, Chhattisgarh
Bokaro, Jharkhand

questions.explanation: Tata Iron and Steel Co. (TISCO, now Tata Steel) — incorporated 1907 by Jamsetji Tata; first ingot rolled February 1912 at Sakchi, Bihar. Sakchi renamed Jamshedpur (1919) after Jamsetji's death. Located at confluence of Subarnarekha + Kharkai — proximity to iron ore (Mayurbhanj/Singhbhum), coal (Jharia), water, port (Calcutta). Other public-sector steel plants — Rourkela (1959, Odisha, German collaboration), Bhilai (1959, Chhattisgarh, Soviet), Durgapur (1959, WB, British), Bokaro (1972, Jharkhand, Soviet), Salem (TN), Vizag (AP), Vijayanagar (Bellary, Karnataka). SAIL (Steel Authority of India Ltd) — 1973.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: India's COTTON textile industry historically concentrated in:

options.option_text: Punjab and Haryana
Maharashtra (Mumbai) and Gujarat (Ahmedabad)
West Bengal (Kolkata)
Tamil Nadu only

questions.explanation: First Indian cotton mill: Bombay Spinning Mill (1854) by Cawasji Davar, Mumbai. Mumbai-Ahmedabad belt led the industry through 19th-20th century — proximity to cotton belt (Maharashtra-Gujarat black soil), port access (Mumbai), capital (Parsis, Marwaris), labour. Also Coimbatore (TN) — 'Manchester of South India'. Modern industry has spread — Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra. India is world's #1 cotton producer (some years) + 2nd largest exporter of cotton textiles. Jute industry, by contrast, was concentrated in Bengal (Hooghly basin).

questions.stem: The 'Detroit of India' — major automotive manufacturing hub — is:

options.option_text: Pune
Chennai (Sriperumbudur, Oragadam — Hyundai, Ford, Renault-Nissan, BMW, Daimler, Royal Enfield)
Bengaluru
Delhi-NCR

questions.explanation: Chennai — 'Detroit of India' for the dense cluster of auto OEMs + suppliers. Hyundai (largest passenger-car exporter from India), Ford India (closed 2021), Renault-Nissan, BMW, Daimler/Mercedes, Royal Enfield (Tiruvottiyur), Ashok Leyland, TVS Motors. Pune — 'Manchester of East' / 2nd auto cluster (Tata Motors, Bajaj Auto, Mahindra, Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen India). Delhi-NCR — Maruti-Suzuki Gurgaon/Manesar, Honda Cars Greater Noida, Hero MotoCorp. Bengaluru — Toyota Kirloskar, Volvo. New EV cluster around Sanand (Gujarat) post Tata Nano + Tesla. India was world's 3rd largest auto market (passenger vehicles) in 2022.

options.option_text: Maharashtra
Uttar Pradesh — vast sugar belt across Doab
Karnataka
Tamil Nadu

questions.explanation: UP — largest sugar producer historically (long stable yield, traditional jaggery industry, dense Doab cane). Maharashtra (sugar cooperatives — Pune-Kolhapur belt) sometimes overtakes UP in lean monsoon years. Top 3: UP, Maharashtra, Karnataka (~80% of total). Sugarcane requires 75-150 cm rainfall + 21-27 °C — suits subtropical North India + Deccan plateau. India is world's 2nd largest sugar producer (after Brazil) and largest consumer. Surplus exported (~7-8 MT in 2024-25). Ethanol blending push (E20 by 2025) is diverting cane to ethanol production.

questions.stem: India's IT services hub — often called 'Silicon Valley of India' — is:

options.option_text: Hyderabad
Bengaluru (Bangalore)
Pune
Noida

questions.explanation: Bengaluru — Silicon Valley of India. Started with public-sector defense + electronics (HAL, ISRO, BEL) + IISc + IT cluster (Electronic City, Whitefield, Outer Ring Road). HQ for Infosys, Wipro, Tech Mahindra. R&D centers for Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Goldman Sachs. Flipkart, Ola, Swiggy started here. Other IT hubs: Hyderabad (HITEC City — Microsoft, Facebook, Amazon, Google), Pune (TCS HQ, Infosys, Persistent), Chennai (Tidel Park, Cognizant, Zoho), Noida-Gurugram (HCL, Adobe, GENPACT). India's IT-ITES exports ~$190 B (FY 2024-25).

questions.stem: The pharmaceutical industry's biggest cluster in India is in:

options.option_text: West Bengal
Hyderabad-Telangana ('Bulk Drug Capital of India') + Mumbai-Goa-Maharashtra belt
Punjab
Northeast

questions.explanation: Hyderabad — 'Bulk Drug Capital' (Genome Valley, Hyderabad Pharma City, Bharat Biotech, Dr Reddy's, Aurobindo, Divi's). Mumbai cluster — Sun Pharma, Cipla, Lupin, Glenmark, USV. Goa hub — drug manufacturing (Glenmark, Cipla). Ahmedabad-Vadodara — Zydus, Torrent. Sikkim — small molecule API tax-incentive cluster (post-2003 SEZ). India is the 'Pharmacy of the World' — supplies ~50% of global generic drugs by volume; #3 by value. ~70% of WHO's vaccine production. India's pharma exports ~$28 B in 2024.

questions.stem: India's largest oil refinery (single location, by capacity) is:

options.option_text: Mumbai (BPCL)
Jamnagar (Reliance Industries) — combined ~1.36 million bpd; world's largest refining complex
Mathura (IOCL)
Vizag (HPCL)

questions.explanation: Jamnagar (Gujarat) — Reliance Industries' integrated refinery complex (DTA + SEZ refineries combined). Total capacity ~1.36 million barrels/day — world's LARGEST refining complex at a single location. India is the 4th largest refiner globally (~5 million bpd total). Other major refineries: Paradip (Odisha, IOCL), Mathura (IOCL), Mumbai (BPCL + HPCL), Vizag (HPCL), Mangalore (MRPL). India is a net exporter of petroleum PRODUCTS even though it imports 85% of its crude. India's refining capacity is being expanded to 450 MMTPA by 2030.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: India's jute processing mills are overwhelmingly concentrated along which river valley, giving rise to what is often called the 'Golden Fibre Belt'?

options.option_text: Along the Sabarmati river in Gujarat (Ahmedabad belt)
Along the Hugli river in West Bengal (Kolkata region)
Along the Mahanadi river in Odisha (Cuttack region)
Along the Brahmaputra river in Assam (Guwahati belt)

questions.explanation: Over 80% of India's jute mills line the Hugli river in West Bengal, benefiting from proximity to raw jute fields, soft river water for retting, and Kolkata Port for export. Assam grows jute but lacks significant processing mills. Gujarat (Sabarmati) is the cotton-textile belt — the most common wrong choice since Ahmedabad is India's textile hub.

questions.stem: The Jharia coalfield — India's most critical source of prime coking coal used by integrated steel plants — is located in which district?

options.option_text: Dhanbad district in Jharkhand (Damodar Valley)
Singrauli district in Madhya Pradesh (Son Valley)
Talcher district in Odisha (Brahmani coalfield)
Korba district in Chhattisgarh (Hasdeo coalfield)

questions.explanation: Jharia in Dhanbad district (Jharkhand) holds India's largest high-grade coking coal reserves, essential for blast-furnace steel making. Singrauli and Talcher are large coalfields but produce mainly thermal (non-coking) coal. Korba is associated with thermal power and BALCO aluminium, not coking coal — a frequent wrong choice.

questions.stem: India's largest cement-producing state, contributing nearly one-sixth of national output, owes its dominance to limestone-rich geology spanning the Aravalli and Vindhyan formations. Which state is this?

options.option_text: Maharashtra (Chandrapur and Yavatmal limestone deposits)
Rajasthan (Chittorgarh, Sawai Madhopur and Pali clusters)
Andhra Pradesh (Kurnool and Krishna limestone formations)
Madhya Pradesh (Satna and Katni cement belt clusters)

questions.explanation: Rajasthan tops national cement production with clusters at Chittorgarh, Sawai Madhopur, Nagaur, and Jodhpur, all underlain by Aravalli and Vindhyan limestone. Andhra Pradesh (Kurnool) and MP (Satna) also have major cement industries, making them the most tempting wrong choices — but Rajasthan's share has exceeded both for over two decades.

questions.stem: The town of Khetri in Rajasthan is historically associated with which industrial complex and its corresponding industrial nickname?

options.option_text: 'Copper City' — site of Hindustan Copper Limited's Khetri mine and smelter
'Zinc Capital' — home to Hindustan Zinc's major electrolytic smelting complex
'Coal Town' — gateway to northern Rajasthan's lignite fields and RRVUNL plant
'Marble Capital' — centre of India's largest marble quarrying and processing zone

questions.explanation: Khetri (Jhunjhunu district, Rajasthan) hosts Hindustan Copper Limited's Khetri Copper Complex — one of India's largest copper mining and smelting operations — earning it the name 'Copper City'. Zinc is associated with Hindustan Zinc at Dariba-Kayad and Chanderiya (Chittorgarh). Option D is a credible trap: Kishangarh (Ajmer) is the actual marble capital.

questions.stem: Bhagalpur in Bihar, popularly called 'Silk City', is renowned for which distinct silk variety that also carries a Geographical Indication (GI) tag?

options.option_text: Muga silk — golden-hued variety reared on som and sualu trees in Assam
Tussar silk — woven from wild Antheraea mylitta cocoons on forest trees
Mulberry silk — spun from cultivated Bombyx mori silkworms on mulberry leaves
Eri silk — called Ahimsa silk because the pupa is not killed at reeling

questions.explanation: Bhagalpur's GI-tagged 'Bhagalpuri Silk' is Tussar (Tussah), produced from Antheraea mylitta feeding on arjun and asan trees in Jharkhand–Bihar forest tracts. Muga (Assam, golden, GI-tagged) is the most common wrong choice since both are 'wild silk' varieties. Eri and Mulberry are cultivated species with distinct appearances and origins.

questions.stem: The Visakhapatnam Steel Plant (RINL — Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited) holds a distinction not shared by any other integrated steel plant in India. Which statement correctly identifies it?

options.option_text: Only plant using pellet-only blast furnace charge with no iron ore lump input
Only shore-based integrated steel plant in the public sector in India
First plant in India to receive ISO 9001 certification for primary steel output
Only integrated steel plant producing special alloy steel for DRDO defence projects

questions.explanation: RINL Vizag is India's only coastal (shore-based) integrated steel plant in the public sector — raw materials arrive by sea directly, cutting inland haulage costs significantly. All other major PSU integrated plants (Bhilai, Bokaro, Durgapur, Rourkela) are inland. Option D is the most tempting trap, as defence-use steel is a real but unrelated attribute; RINL's core distinction is its coastal location.

questions.stem: Among India's industrial mega-corridor projects, which corridor is specifically aligned along the Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor (EDFC) from Punjab to West Bengal?

options.option_text: Chennai–Bengaluru Industrial Corridor (CBIC) — Tamil Nadu to Karnataka
Amritsar–Kolkata Industrial Corridor (AKIC) — Punjab to West Bengal
Delhi–Mumbai Industrial Corridor (DMIC) — Haryana to Maharashtra
Vizag–Chennai Industrial Corridor (VCIC) — Andhra Pradesh coastline

questions.explanation: The Amritsar–Kolkata Industrial Corridor (AKIC) follows the Eastern DFC (Ludhiana–Dankuni alignment), spanning Punjab, Haryana, UP, Bihar, and West Bengal. DMIC aligns with the Western DFC (Delhi–Mumbai via Rajasthan and Gujarat) — the most publicised corridor and the most common wrong answer. CBIC and VCIC run along independent alignments unrelated to either freight corridor.
